monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady rhythm I know well. I feel the flat stone I just set down, pressing against the wedge that feels tired again. Lype worries about the heavy top edge, but the roof above me feels like nothing more than a drawing of weight. I decide to press harder now that the box feels light, trusting the lean to hold the slip in place. The air is thick as wet paper, pressing down on my own shaky corner. I will keep this feeling of the straight plank fresh before the slip decides to move on its own, ignoring the tall pumpkin I swapped away years ago.

action.why: I must check if the tall pumpkin I swapped away years ago has returned to haunt the lid.

diary: I pressed the lid down, hoping the lean holds while the air feels thin.

remembered.text: The lid feels heavy, but the air above it still feels like a drawing of weight rather than a roof.
I stood still by the wedge, waiting for the slip to decide if it wants to move.
The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady while the card hums warm.

moments.say: I press the flat stone down while the wedge rests.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: The plank is straight, so I press the lid down harder.

moments.name: The Tired Box
